body.p: I. Status of the Claims
By this Reply, Applicant amends claims 1, 9, and 17. The originally filed
specification, e.g., paragraph [0046], and drawings fully support the subject matter of the amended and new claims. No new matter has been added. II. Section 112(b) Rejections
In the Office Action, claims 1-20 were rejected as indefinite under 35 U.S.C.

§ 112(b) based on the use of the phrase "a healthy or average blood flow characteristic" recited in each of claims 1, 9, and 17. (Office Action at p.2.) While Applicant does not agree that this phrase renders the claims unclear, to further prosecution, Applicant has amended each of independent claims 1, 9, and 17 to recite, "a predetermined healthy or average blood flow characteristic based on a population-based measurement or estimate." Support for this feature can be found at least at paragraph [0046] of the specification as filed.

This phrase in each of independent claims 1, 9, and 17 is clear and definite. For example, the characteristic of the claims is "based on a population-based measurement or estimate." While this feature may be broad since different populations may be used to determine the measurement or estimate, the breadth of the claim should not be confused with indefiniteness. MPEP 2173.04. Accordingly, withdrawal of the Section 112(b) rejections is respectfully submitted. III. Section 103 Rejections
In the Office Action, claims 1-20 which were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over one or more of Taylor (U.S. Publication No.

2012/0041318 Al), Mabotuwana et al. ("A model of blood flow in the mesenteric arterial system" Biomed Eng Onlin. 2007), Walker ("Mesenteric vasculature and collateral pathways" Seminars in interventional radiology vol. 26, 3 (2009): 167-74), Taub et al. (U.S. Publication No. 2012/0088955), and/or Heldt et al. ("Scaling cardiovascular parameters for population simulations." Computers in Cardiology, 2004. IEEE).

Claim 1 recites, in part, "determining a threshold blood flow characteristic based on the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's bowel, the threshold blood flow characteristic comprising a healthy or average blood flow characteristic based on a population-based measurement or estimate." In rejecting claim 1, the Office Action contends that Taylor teaches "a range or threshold of intensity values centered at the selected intensity value." (Office Action at p. 7.) And while the Office Action acknowledges that Taylor fails to teach "determining a threshold blood flow characteristic," the Office Action contends that Taub at Heldt teach this feature and, thus, cure the deficiency of Taylor. (Id. at p. 11.)

Taylor discloses a threshold value for intensity values of an image. (Taylor at para. [0135].) Taub discloses determining a threshold suction flow rate based on fluid flowing through a device 200. (Para. [0230].) The Office Action asserts that Heldt discloses setting parameters, generating steady-state values, and compare to the model's prediction. (Office Action at p. 11.) None of these references, however, discloses determining a threshold based on the patient-specific model, and having the threshold including characteristics associated with a healthy population. Put another way, none of the references determine a threshold using both characteristics associated with a healthy population and the patient-specific model.

For at least the foregoing reasons, independent claim 1 and claims dependent therefrom are patentably distinguishable over the applied art. While of different scope, independent claims 9 and 17 recite similarly distinguishing features as discussed above relative to independent claim 1. Thus, independent claims 9 and 17, and claims dependent therefrom, are patentably distinguishable over the applied art at least for the foregoing reasons.
IV. After Final Consideration Pilot

Applicant requests that this application be considered under the After Final Consideration Pilot Program 2.0 at the USPTO. A Certification and Request for Consideration Under the After Final Consideration Pilot Program 2.0 is being filed herewith. Applicant appreciates the Examiner's consideration of this Reply under that Program.
V. Conclusion

The Office Action contains characterizations of the claims and the related art with which the applicant does not necessarily agree. Unless expressly noted otherwise, applicant declines to subscribe to any statement or characterization in the Office Action.
In discussing the specification, claims, and drawings in this Reply, it is to be

understood that Applicant is in no way intending to limit the scope of the claims to any exemplary embodiments described in the specification or abstract and/or shown in the drawings. Rather, Applicant is entitled to have the claims interpreted broadly to the maximum extent permitted by statute, regulation, and applicable case law.
Applicant respectfully requests that this Reply under 37 C.F.R. § 1.116 be
entered by the Examiner, placing the claims in condition for allowance. The proposed
claim amendments do not raise new issues or necessitate the undertaking of any additional search of the art by the Examiner. Therefore, this Reply should allow for immediate action by the Examiner.
Furthermore, Applicant respectfully points out that the final Office Action

presented new arguments as to the application of the art against the pending claims. It is respectfully submitted that the entering of this Reply would allow Applicant to respond to the final rejection and place the application in condition for allowance.
Finally, Applicant submits that the entry of this Reply would place the application in better form for appeal, should the Examiner dispute the patentability of the pending claims.

In view of the foregoing remarks, Applicant submits that this claimed invention is neither anticipated nor rendered obvious in view of the prior art references cited against this application. Applicant therefore requests the reconsideration and reexamination of the application, and the timely allowance of the pending claims.
